Myths on Clay retells the great stories of Hindu tradition in the style of Rajput and Pahari miniature paintings. Hinduism is a living religion followed by more than a billion people, and many of these stories are sacred to them: we tell them as the texts tell them, and we always say which text we follow, because the Vedas, the Puranas and the epics often tell the same story in different ways.
Sources: Rig Veda (trans. Jamison & Brereton, 2014); Shatapatha Brahmana (trans. Julius Eggeling); Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana (trans. H. H. Wilson); Shiva Purana; Linga Purana; Mahabharata (critical edition, trans. van Buitenen); Kalidasa, Kumarasambhava. Further reading: Wendy Doniger, Hindu Myths: A Sourcebook; Dimmitt & van Buitenen, Classical Hindu Mythology; Heinrich Zimmer, Myths and Symbols in Indian Art and Civilization.
Narrated by Matías.
